background_notes.fact: For A>0 and r>0, Fourier projections contract every H^s norm, ||P_(>A)u||_(H^(-r))<=A^(-r)||u||_2 and ||P_(>A)u||_2<=A^(-1)||u||_(H^1). For N>=2, ||P_(<=N) partial_x^2 u||_2<=N^2||u||_2. These projections commute with the multipliers S_t, Dinv and spatial derivatives.

grounds.reason: Sobolev norms are weighted Fourier square sums and projections retain the stated frequencies.
S_t is a scalar multiplier at each frequency.
Spatial derivatives and Dinv are scalar Fourier multipliers.
The threshold is an arbitrary real N>=2; the bounds are applied to smooth periodic paths and J outputs in H^1.

background_notes.justification: Deleting summands contracts the nonnegative weighted square sums. On |k|>A, <k>^(-r)<=A^(-r) and <k>^(-1)<=A^(-1); on |k|<=N, |k|^2<=N^2. Squaring these pointwise inequalities and summing gives the bounds. Diagonal multipliers commute. Consequently N005's Dinv P(FG) estimate yields the stated N^2 low-frequency bound, since partial_x(FG)=partial_x^2 Dinv P(FG).

background_notes.fact: The trilinear operator Cint has output frequency k=k1+k2+k3. Thus P_(>N)Cint(P_(<=N/3)f1,P_(<=N/3)f2,P_(<=N/3)f3)=0. Fixed spatial projections commute with weak time differentiation and contract X on every subinterval.

grounds.reason: Cint is formed from two spatial products and Fourier multipliers.
The projections retain the specified Fourier frequencies.
X uses an L2 supremum and a negative Sobolev weak derivative supremum.
N006 supplies Cint on paths with the required finite X norms.
The proof explicitly decomposes all three inputs at N/3.

background_notes.justification: Each retained input frequency has modulus <=N/3, so each resulting product frequency has modulus <=N by the triangle inequality; S, P and Dinv never change a frequency. The low-frequency projected inputs have finite Fourier support, so this support assertion needs no interchange of infinite products or integrals. Multilinearity gives the three remaining terms exactly as displayed. Bounded fixed linear projections commute with distributional time differentiation by testing the weak derivative identity, and contraction follows from the Fourier norm sums. Restriction to a shorter interval cannot increase either supremum.

value.definition: mathbbT=ℝ/(2*pi*ℤ), with normalized measure dx/(2*pi).

For a periodic integrable f, hat f(k)=(2*pi)^(-1) integral_0^(2*pi) f(x) exp(-i*k*x) dx. The transform extends by completion to Sobolev spaces and by distributional duality. Reality means hat f(-k)=conjugate(hat f(k)); mean zero means hat f(0)=0.

value.type: family of Fourier Sobolev spaces and norms
value.definition: For real s, <k>=(1+k^2)^(1/2), ||f||_(H^s)^2=sum_(k in Z) <k>^(2*s)|hat f(k)|^2. H^s is the completion of trigonometric polynomials, interpreted as distributions for negative s; L2=H^0 with the normalized spatial norm. On mean-zero functions ||f||_(dot H^s)^2=sum_(k!=0)|k|^(2*s)|hat f(k)|^2. Time suprema use continuous representatives and derivative norms essential suprema. For sequences x, ||x||_(ell2)^2=sum_k |x(k)|^2; ell1 uses sum_k |x(k)|. Frequency projections P_{<=A}, P_{>A} retain respectively |k|<=A and |k|>A.
S_t=exp(-t*partial_x^3), hat(S_t f)(k)=exp(i*t*k^3)*hat f(k), for every real t.
P0 f=hat f(0), identified with the constant function.
P=I-P0.
Dinv=D^(-1)=partial_x^(-1): its multiplier is (i*k)^(-1) at k!=0 and zero at k=0. D^(-2)=Dinv composed with Dinv. Spatial derivatives use multiplier i*k.
For tau>0 and periodic f in L2, F_tau(f)=(1/6)*P[(S_tau Dinv f)^2]-(1/6)*S_tau P[(Dinv f)^2].

For tau>0 and periodic f in L2, H_tau(f)=(1/3)*P[(S_tau Dinv f)*Dinv F_tau(f)]+(tau/9)*(S_tau Dinv f)*P0(f^2)-(1/54)*[S_(tau-s) Dinv[(S_s Dinv f)^3]]_(s=0)^(s=tau)-(1/(27*tau))*[S_(tau-s) D^(-2)[(S_(s-tau) D^(-2) F_tau(f))*(S_s Dinv f)]]_(s=0)^(s=tau). Every product is spatial and [G(s)]_0^tau=G(tau)-G(0).

value.definition: Psi_tau(f)=S_tau f+F_tau(f)+H_tau(f). For positive integer L set tau=T/L and t_n=n*tau. Define u^0=u0 and u^(n+1)=Psi_tau(u^n) for 0<=n<L. There is no spatial cutoff in this recurrence.
For tau>0, M_tau g=tau^(-1) integral_0^tau g(s)ds and eta_tau(alpha,beta)=M_tau(exp(-i*s*(alpha+beta)))-M_tau(exp(-i*s*alpha))*M_tau(exp(-i*s*beta)).

For tau>0, t_n=n*tau and k!=0, hat(R2_(n,tau)(f1,f2,f3))(k)= -tau/(18*i*k) sum_(a+b+c=k,a+b!=0) exp(-i*t_n*Phi)*eta_tau(alpha,beta)*hat f1(a)*hat f2(b)*hat f3(c), with p=a+b, alpha=3*a*b*p, beta=3*k*c*p, Phi=alpha+beta=k^3-a^3-b^3-c^3. Output at k=0 is zero. Initially this formula is on Fourier polynomials; bounded extension is proved below. Terms with a zero input frequency vanish since one phase is zero.
B_t(f,g)=S_(-t) partial_x[(S_t f)(S_t g)].
J_t(f,g)=S_(-t) P[(S_t Dinv f)(S_t Dinv g)].

p_star=23/14. For an interval I of length at most one, ||f||_X(I)=||f||_(L^infty(I;L2))+||partial_t f||_(L^infty(I;H^(-p_star))).

value.type: normalized periodic KdV equation and exact-solution convention
value.definition: KdV is the equation u_t+partial_x^3 u=(1/2)*partial_x(u^2) on mathbbT. For a real mean-zero datum q in H^s, s>=0, and horizon A>0, an exact solution u with datum q means the real mean-zero C([0,A];H^s) distributional solution of this equation with u(0)=q obtained by smooth approximation. An exact twisted solution v means v(t)=S_(-t)u(t) for this same equation and interval. A smooth exact solution means such a solution with smooth space and time dependence. These terms specify a solution relation only; existence, uniqueness, bounds and the differential equation for the twist are proved, rather than granted by this definition.

value.statement: S_t is unitary in every H^s, preserves reality and zero mean. On mean-zero inputs, uniformly in real t: ||Dinv f||_(H^1)+||Dinv f||_infty<=C||f||_2; ||B_t(f,g)||_(H^(-23/14))<=C||f||_2||g||_2; ||J_t(f,g)||_(H^1)<=C||f||_2||g||_2. For every A0 in H^1, ||A0||_infty<=C||A0||_(H^1). For A0,B0 in H^1, ||A0 B0||_(H^1)<=C||A0||_(H^1)||B0||_(H^1). Also ||Dinv P(FG)||_2<=C||F||_2||G||_2, ||A0||_(H^(-23/14))<=||Dinv A0||_2 for mean-zero A0, and ||J_t(A0,B0)||_2<=C||Dinv A0||_2||B0||_2 whenever the right side is defined. For smooth mean-zero paths f,g on [a,b], integral_a^b B_t(f,g)dt=(1/3)[J_t(f,g)]_a^b-(1/3)integral_a^b[J_t(f',g)+J_t(f,g')]dt. Moreover J is symmetric and integral_I J_t(B_t(f,g),h)dt=Cint_I(f,g,h). These identities hold stepwise for piecewise smooth paths, and Stage_(n,tau)(t;f)=[J_s(f,f)]_(s=n*tau)^t/6.

argument.text: Fix any smooth real mean-zero solution u of u_t+u_xxx=(1/2)*partial_x(u^2) on [0,T], the normalized KdV equation of D020, and define v(t)=S_(-t)u(t). Take its numerical interpolation V with residual Rres. Put M=1+sup||v||_(H^gamma), e=v-V and fix I=[a,b] starting at a grid point, h=b-a<=1, 0<tau<=1. Assume L1: E_I=sup_I||e||_2<=1. At each step intersecting I use f=v^n=V(t_n), w=v(t_n), delta_n=||f-w||_2<=E_I and q_n=tau^gamma+delta_n. N007 supplies the actual residual identity and grid values, and N009 gives sup||rho_n||_2<=C_M tau q_n and ||Rres'||_(L^infty H^(-p_star))<=C_M q_n. There are at most h/tau+1 intersected steps (including a final partial step). Hence sup_(a<=t<=b)||Rres(t)-Rres(a)||_2<=C_M(h+tau)(tau^gamma+E_I). For the exact path, D004 gives partial_t S_(-t)=partial_x^3 S_(-t), commuting with spatial derivatives. Thus v'=S_(-t)(u_t+u_xxx)=(1/2)S_(-t)partial_x(u^2)=(1/2)B_t(v,v), since S_t v=u. Smoothness justifies this differentiation and the spatial products. Subtracting N007's identity V'=B_t(V,V)/2+Rres' and using symmetry and bilinearity gives e'=(B_t(v,v)-B_t(V,V))/2-Rres'=B_t(e,(v+V)/2)-Rres'=B_t(e,v-e/2)-Rres'. N005 then gives ||e||_X(I)<=C_M(tau^gamma+E_I), and ||v||_X(I)+||V||_X(I)<=C_M. Here V=v-e, and the exact solution has L2 norm <=M throughout.

Define FI(t)=integral_a^t B_s(e,v-e/2)ds. Integration gives e(t)=e(a)+FI(t)-(Rres(t)-Rres(a)). Fix N>=2 only for analysis. For low frequencies N005's bound ||Dinv P(FG)||_2<=C||F||_2||G||_2, followed by two powers of frequency on |k|<=N, gives sup_I||P_(<=N)FI||_2<=C_M N^2 h E_I. For high frequencies apply the normal form in N005 with g=v-e/2, retaining both endpoints. Since e'=B(e,g)-Rres' and g'=B(v,v)/2-B(e,g)/2+Rres'/2, symmetry of J and the cubic identity give exactly FI(t)=[J_s(e,g)]_a^t/3-Cint_[a,t](e,g,V)/3-Cint_[a,t](v,v,e)/6+(1/3)integral_a^t J_s(Rres',V)ds. Indeed g-e/2=V combines the first differentiated pair, and -J(Rres',g)+J(e,Rres')/2=-J(Rres',V) before multiplication by -1/3. N005's H^1 bound on J bounds both high-output endpoints by C_M N^(-1)E_I. This includes the initial endpoint when e(a)!=0.

produces.statement: e(t)=e(a)+FI(t)-(Rres(t)-Rres(a)); sup_I||P_(<=N)FI||_2<=C_M N^2 h E_I; FI(t)=[J_s(e,g)]_a^t/3-Cint_[a,t](e,g,V)/3-Cint_[a,t](v,v,e)/6+(1/3)integral_a^t J_s(Rres',V)ds, with g=v-e/2, and the high-output endpoint norm is <=C_M N^(-1)E_I.

argument.text: Let f1,f2,f3 be any three paths of finite X norm on I. For each path decompose frequencies at N/3. If all three input frequencies have modulus <=N/3, their sum has modulus <=N, so that cubic contribution vanishes after P_(>N). Multilinearity writes the remaining contribution as the sum of Cint(P_(>N/3)f1,f2,f3), Cint(P_(<=N/3)f1,P_(>N/3)f2,f3), and Cint(P_(<=N/3)f1,P_(<=N/3)f2,P_(>N/3)f3). Fourier projections contract L2 and the derivative H^(-23/14) norm. Each designated high input has H^(-23/14) norm <=C N^(-23/14) times its L2 norm. N006 therefore bounds this sum by C*h*product_j||f_j||_X+C*N^(-23/14)*product_j||f_j||_(L^infty L2), putting the negative norm on the designated high input in each summand. Instantiate this inequality for (e,g,V) and (v,v,e), where g=v-e/2. F001 gives ||e||_X<=C_M(tau^gamma+E_I), the other X norms <=C_M, and their L2 products <=C_M E_I. Consequently the two projected cubic integrals have total norm <=C_M*h*tau^gamma+C_M*(h+N^(-23/14))*E_I.

For the forcing term in F002 use the actual stepwise Rres' from N007. On each intersected step define again f=v^n, w=v(t_n), delta_n=||f-w||_2 and q_n=tau^gamma+delta_n. On this step the forcing integral is the sum -Cint(Y_n,z_n,V)-Cint(Y_n,Y_n,V)/2-tau^(-1)integral J_s(W_n,V)ds over that intersection. N008 gives ||Y_n||_X<=C_M q_n and ||Y_n||_(L^infty H^(-p_star))<=C_M tau q_n. N006 with the negative norm on Y_n, and F001's bound on V, control each cubic term by C_M tau q_n; for the term with two Y_n use q_n<=2. N008's ||W_n||_2<=C_M tau q_n and N005's L2 bound for J control the last integral by C_M tau q_n, even on a partial step. Summing yields C_M(h+tau)(tau^gamma+E_I). Together with F002-F003 this gives sup||P_(>N)FI||_2<=C_M(h+tau)tau^gamma+C_M(h+tau+N^(-1)+N^(-p_star))E_I. Add the low-frequency estimate and F001's residual bound in the exact error identity. The result is E_I<=||e(a)||_2+C_M(h+tau)tau^gamma+C_M(N^2*h+h+tau+N^(-1)+N^(-23/14))*E_I. Discharge L1.

argument.notes: S001 correctly differentiates v=S_(-t)u and obtains the error equation and F001 using N005/N009. In S002 the differentiated normal form combines g-e/2=V, giving the displayed cubic coefficients and positive residual forcing; both boundary terms are retained.
